components.name: Primary CTA Button
components.description: High-contrast action trigger with sharp rectangular edges and micro-lift hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; background: #18181b; color: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #18181b; padding: 12px 24px; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 0; transition: transform 0.2s ease, opacity 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #18181b; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-arrow { transition: transform 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover .ds-btn-arrow { transform: translateX(4px); }

components.name: Corner Frame Specimen Card
components.description: Photographic container framed by opposing L-shaped mechanical corner ticks.
components.css: .ds-corner-frame { position: relative; background: #e4e4e7; padding: 8px; border-radius: 0; } .ds-corner-frame::before, .ds-corner-frame::after { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 12px; height: 12px; pointer-events: none; border-color: #a1a1aa; } .ds-corner-frame::before { left: 0; top: 0; border-left: 1px solid #a1a1aa; border-top: 1px solid #a1a1aa; } .ds-corner-frame::after { right: 0; bottom: 0; border-right: 1px solid #a1a1aa; border-bottom: 1px solid #a1a1aa; } .ds-corner-content { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16/10; background: #ffffff; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: #52525b; }

components.name: Kicker Eyebrow
components.description: Uppercase monospace metadata label identifying category or taxonomy.
components.css: .ds-kicker { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.16em; color: #71717a; margin: 0; }

components.name: Section Header Split
components.description: Asymmetric layout: kicker and bold display title on left, narrative on right, sealed by a 1px hairline.
components.html:
LABORATORY OVERVIEW

Robotics & Intelligent Systems

components.css: .ds-section-header { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid #e4e4e7; padding-bottom: 24px; margin-bottom: 32px; } @media (min-width: 768px) { .ds-section-header { flex-direction: row; align-items: flex-end; justify-content: space-between; } } .ds-kicker { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.16em; color: #71717a; margin: 0 0 8px 0; } .ds-heading { font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif; font-size: 32px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.05; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #18181b; margin: 0; } .ds-narrative { font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; color: #52525b; line-height: 1.6; max-width: 380px; margin: 0; }

narrative.overview:
The B401 Robotics Laboratory design system is built on the aesthetic and mechanical discipline of technical engineering blueprints and physical laboratory instruments. The interface prioritizes clarity, informational density, and high-contrast readability. Every visual element communicates structural intent: stark monochrome zinc surfaces, razor-thin 1px architectural hairlines, technical monospace metadata kickers, and mechanical L-shaped corner framing ticks.

Rather than decorative embellishment, the system achieves distinction through precise proportions, deliberate typographic contrast, and restrained motion. Display headlines are rendered in geometric, bold Poppins to establish presence, anchored by a neutral DM Sans reading body, and cataloged via wide-tracked monospace tags.

Anti-reference: Consumer SaaS slop. The interface rejects saturated purple/indigo gradient buttons, pill-shaped bubble badges, noisy decorative drop shadows, and artificial glassmorphism. Surfaces are flat, intentional, and strictly grounded in authentic laboratory evidence.
keyCharacteristics: Strict architectural flatness bounded by 1px hairline dividers.
L-shaped corner ticks enclosing specimen cards, robotic hardware photos, and project assets.
Monochrome blueprint zinc palette with functional status signaling only.
High-contrast typography pairing Poppins display, DM Sans body, and monospace label scales.
Clean technical affordances with sharp right-angle geometries.

rules.name: The Zero-Gradient Rule
rules.body: Gradients are strictly forbidden across backgrounds, text, and buttons. Visual hierarchy is achieved exclusively through scale, weight, and tonal contrast.

rules.name: The Functional Color Rule
rules.body: Chromatic color may never be used for decoration. Red is permitted only for error states; green and amber are permitted only for verified operational status.

rules.name: The Kicker Precedence Rule
rules.body: Every major section heading must be preceded by an uppercase monospace kicker establishing context or taxonomy before the title is read.

rules.name: The Solid Heading Rule
rules.body: Display headings remain solid high-contrast foreground color; secondary muted words are reserved only for deliberate secondary sub-phrases.

rules.name: The Hairline Boundary Rule
rules.body: Never separate flat content blocks with shadow elevation; always delineate boundaries with a 1px solid hairline border.

dos: Do precede major section headings with a monospace uppercase kicker.
Do enclose hardware images and research specimen photography inside .corner-frame containers with L-shaped corner ticks.
Do enforce sharp 0px radius on buttons, inputs, tags, and content cards.
Do use 1px hairlines (border-zinc-200 dark:border-white/10) for all spatial dividers and borders.
Do maintain strict monochrome zinc tones for all layout surfaces and typography.
donts: Don't use purple, indigo, cyan, or rainbow gradient fills on buttons, backgrounds, or text.
Don't introduce bubbly rounded pill buttons or high-radius cards.
Don't apply heavy diffuse drop shadows to resting cards.
Don't use color decoratively; reserve chromatic red exclusively for error conditions and alerts.
Don't omit dark mode support for any new component or view.
